terms.grammar: phrase: cōnstō with the ablative of price
evidence: Sen. Ep. 17.4: parvō famēs cōnstat, magnō fastīdium
Traupman 130: cheaply, parvō or vīlī pretiō
Traupman 131: at a high price, magnō
terms.comment: With verbs of buying, selling and costing, the price is in the ablative: magnō, parvō, plūrimō, minimō, vīlī. Only tantī, quantī, plūris, minōris are genitive (see below and how much is it?).

terms.grammar: phrase: cōnstō with the genitive of price; so also tantī, quantī
evidence: Cic. Att. 13.29.2: prope dīmidiō minōris cōnstābit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Quantī cōnstat?, how much does it cost?; tantī, at that price.

evidence: Traupman 130 (to cost a lot, little …: the genitive)
terms.comment: The genitives magnī, parvī are for valuing (magnī aestimāre, see value); for costing, Lewis & Short gives the ablative, and the genitive only for tantī, quantī, plūris, minōris.

phrases.english: hunger costs little, fussiness a lot
I don’t buy regret at that price

sources: Lewis & Short: consto
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): p. 130; p. 289.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. expensive.
